method: Evidence/rights gates first. Placement blends interest, relevance, novelty, familiarity, consequence, source confidence, originality, visual strength, freshness, radar context and rotation pressure, then applies a diversity rerank so nearby homepage slots prefer different categories and subjects. Editorial story-overrides are applied before ranking so approved headlines and imagery persist across generated homepage surfaces.

feature.headline: Four Burlington technologies that ended up around the world
feature.deck: Water treatment systems, laboratory robots, broadcast hardware and plant-based materials all have deep Burlington roots.
feature.label: Made in Burlington
feature.alt: Illustration linking Burlington to water, laboratory, broadcast and bio-based technologies around the world.
feature.storyGoal: Show Burlington's global technology footprint through four verified examples whose products or systems are used around the world.

feature.headline: Oakville approved a new Costco near Burloak. How will drivers get in?

feature.storyGoal: Explain the recently approved Costco site plan near Burloak through the practical questions Burlington drivers care about: status, parking, access and what is still unconfirmed.

feature.storyGoal: Help Burlington readers understand what the best comparable crime data actually says, and where a regional score cannot answer a city-level question.

feature.headline: Up to 90% of a building can now be made inside this Burlington factory.
feature.deck: A $15-million Canadian hub is changing how some schools, homes and care buildings could be assembled.
feature.label: Made in Burlington
feature.alt: A building under construction in an industrial factory setting.
feature.storyGoal: Turn a new investment announcement into an understandable Made in Burlington story about what the factory makes, how much work can happen indoors and the scale SEKISUI says it is targeting.

rail.headline: Can you have a backyard fire pit in Burlington?
rail.deck: A wood fire for sitting around is generally not allowed in urban Burlington. Propane and cooking fires are treated differently.
rail.label: Home rules
rail.alt: People gathered around a backyard wood fire pit at dusk.
rail.storyGoal: Explain the Burlington backyard-fire rule in plain language, including the urban wood-fire ban, cooking exception, propane and natural-gas exception, and rural permit system.

rail.headline: Which Burlington intersection is actually the worst?
rail.deck: The public records point to a larger problem along one of Burlington's busiest roads.
rail.label: Road safety
rail.alt: Illustration of a damaged car and motorcycle at an intersection; not a photograph of a collision discussed in this article.
rail.storyGoal: Use collision counts, red-light camera totals and engineering records to explain why Burlington's worst intersection changes by the measure used, and why different problems keep appearing along Guelph Line.

rail.headline: Do you need a permit for a shed in Burlington?
rail.deck: Not always. The building-permit threshold is 15 square metres, but a small shed still has to follow zoning rules.
rail.label: Home rules
rail.alt: Two people building a wooden shed in a residential backyard.
rail.storyGoal: Answer the Burlington shed-permit question directly, then separate the 15-square-metre building-permit exemption from zoning and property-specific approvals.
